addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>

Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop

- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR

- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- plugin-dev:agent-development: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create an agent", "add an agent", "write a subagent", "agent frontmatter", "when to use description", "agent examples", "agent tools", "agent colors", "autonomous agent", or needs guidance on agent structure, system prompts, triggering conditions, or agent development best practices for Claude Code plugins.

I'm requesting changes on a few items before merge. One of them is a genuine architecture decision that's really yours to make, since you own both the code and the integration doc.

### Must Resolve Before Merge

**1. The Contentful preview (CPA) token is reaching the browser.**
In both `contentfulPreview/index.tsx` and `experience/index.tsx`, the client is built client-side with the preview token and points at `preview.contentful.com` directly. Since `config/default.js` (~L186–190) serializes `previewAccessToken` into the same bundle as the delivery token, on any environment where `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` is set the token ships to the browser — where it can be lifted and used to read every unpublished draft in the space.

This contradicts our confirmed integration doc `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9: *"CPA token held server-side in MRT; never reaches the browser; requests proxied through an MRT preview endpoint."*

Same root cause, related: in `experience/index.tsx`, `resolvedToken` prefers the preview token even when `isPreview` is false — so normal `/:slug` traffic hits the preview host and can serve drafts on any env with the token set.

Since you own both the code and that doc, the real question is intent:
- If client-side preview is a deliberate call (Studio licence, simpler) → let's update §3/§4/§9 to match, add a hard "non-prod only" gate on the token, and get it signed off.
- If not → route the draft fetch through an MRT proxy so the token stays server-side (the doc's design).

**2. The `/preview` route is ungated on production and not `noindex`.**
`routes.tsx` registers it unconditionally with SSR on, so it's live and crawlable on the customer site — SEO duplicate-content risk, and it's the missing safety net that would turn a stray prod preview-token into a public draft leak. Gate it to preview environments (e.g. 404 when there's no preview token) and add `noindex`. This mostly rides along with whichever option we pick for #1.

### Should-Fix
- `experience/index.tsx`: `useFetchBySlug` is called after the `if (!client) return`, which breaks the Rules of Hooks. The new preview page already shows the right pattern (fetch inside a child component) — mirror it here.
- `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`: drop the `console.log` — we don't have a project logger yet, so remove rather than replace.
- `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`: the `getEntry` effect can let a stale response overwrite a newer one — add a cancel guard and clear state on `entry`/`locale` change.
- Both pages duplicate the client-creation logic — worth extracting into one shared hook, which is also the single place the #1 fix should live.

### Non-Blocking / Unrelated
- `.mcp.json` adds `b2c-dx-mcp` pinned to `@latest` with `--allow-non-ga-tools`, project-wide. It's unrelated to preview — I'd split it into its own PR, and pin a version either way. (CodeRabbit flagged this one as Major.)

### CodeRabbit Cross-Check
I re-ran a full CodeRabbit review to verify, and it independently surfaced the same core findings — the client-side preview token, the `/:slug` draft-leak, the Rules-of-Hooks issue, the `console.log`, the race condition, and the `.mcp.json` pin — and it also landed on **Request changes**. content.content:
=== ISSUE/PR #42 ===
{"body":"## Summary

- New workflow `sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml` — triggered manually from GitHub Actions → Run workflow
- No hardcoded variable names: reads `.env.sample` for the key list, fetches actual values from the selected GitHub Environment via the GitHub API, then intersects the two
- Only keys that are **set and non-empty** in the GitHub Environment are PATCHed to MRT — missing keys are silently skipped so MRT retains existing values
- `scope:personal` and `scope:auto` keys (including `ENVIRONMENT_NAME`) are never synced
- Supports **dry run** mode — shows exactly what would be synced without touching MRT

## How it works

```
.env.sample  →  parse scope:shared + scope:tier keys
                        ↓
GitHub API   →  GET /environments/{target}/variables  (all set vars)
                        ↓
intersection →  keys in both + non-empty value
                        ↓
MRT API      →  PATCH /projects/zimmermann/target/{target}/env-var/
```

## Usage

**GitHub Actions → Workflows → "Sync Env Vars to MRT" → Run workflow**

Select target (`dev` / `test` / `sit` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) and optionally enable dry run.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run with `dry_run: true` for `dev` — verify output lists the expected keys without calling MRT
- [ ] Run with `dry_run: false` for `dev` — verify MRT target shows updated values in Runtime Admin
- [ ] Add a new key to `.env.sample` — verify it appears in the next sync 
=== ISSUE/PR #43 ===
{"body":"## Summary

- Adds `/preview` route (`ContentfulPreview`) for Contentful Studio live preview — gated to non-prod environments (returns 404 when `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_ACCESS_TOKEN` is absent, so the route is inert on staging/prod)
- Adds `?preview` query-param support on Experience pages, falling back to delivery mode silently when no CPA token is configured
- Extracts `ExperienceFetch` child component to fix a React hooks violation (conditional `useFetchBySlug` call)
- Adds `<Seo noIndex />` on both preview paths so draft content is never indexed
- Adds shared constants to `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`
- Updates `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9 to document the deliberate client-side CPA token tradeoff

## Changed files

| File | Tier | Owner | Reviewer required? |
|------|------|-------|-------------------|
| `overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad B | No |
| `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` | Tier 4 | Squad B | No |
| `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` | Tier 1 | Integration/SI Partner | Yes — Tier 1 change (read-only config addition) |
| `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` | Tier 4 | — | No |

> **Tier 1 note:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` is Tier 1 (runtime/integration config). This PR only adds new exported constants — no existing config logic is modified. CODEOWNERS will auto-request `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` review.

## Security note — CPA t

aiTitle: Investigate closed PR #41 and deployment to dev

content.text:
## PR #41 — Full Report

**Bottom line:** PR #41 is legitimately closed (never merged — `mergedAt`/`mergedBy` are both null). It was closed by the author and replaced 20 minutes later by **PR #43** (same branch, still open), which fixes the two blocking issues your review raised that the last commit on #41 didn't. The "deployed to dev" you saw isn't tied to a merge — this repo auto-deploys to the shared `dev` MRT environment on **every push to the branch**, regardless of PR/review state, and pushes to that branch continued under #43 after #41 closed.

### Timeline

| When (2026-07-) | Event |
|---|---|
| 24, 01:19 | Mani (`mani060689`) opens PR #41, `feature/storefront-preview-contentful` → `develop`. Adds `/preview` route for Contentful Live Preview + preview support on Experience pages. Reviewers auto-requested: PWA Squad A, PWA Squad B, Tier-2 Approvers, Tier-1 Approvers (touches `routes.tsx`, a Tier-2 Global Shell file). |
| 24, 01:19 | `github-actions[bot]` posts the Tier 2 Protected Files warning on `routes.tsx`. |
| 24, 01:20–01:43 | Three commits pushed; each auto-deploys to `dev` (`deployed` events at 01:20, 01:40, 01:43 — this is the auto-deploy-on-push behavior, not a review-gated release). |
| 24, 01:41 | CodeRabbit's **first full review passes clean → APPROVED**. |
| 24, 01:41 | `TimLavelleACC` comments, pings CodeRabbit after assigning a reviewer. |
| 27, 05:49 | **You** trigger `@coderabbitai full-review`. |
| 27, 05:53 | CodeRabbit comes back **CHANGES_REQUESTED** this time — 6 actionable findings: CPA (preview) token reachable client-side, unpinned `@latest` on the new `b2c-dx-mcp` MCP server, a Rules-of-Hooks violation in `experience/index.tsx`, a stray `console.log`, a stale-request race in the preview page's `useEffect`, and the token-preference bug on normal `/:slug` traffic. |
| 27, 07:26 | **You** post a formal **Requesting Changes** review — the substantive one. See below. |
| 28, 04:28 | Mani pushes `9d0cd8c` — *"fix(contentful): address CodeRabbit review on PR #41"* — and separately posts a review comment. |
| 28, 04:29 | Auto-deploy to `dev` fires again for that commit. |
| 28, 05:21 | Mani re-triggers `@coderabbitai review`. CodeRabbit replies it doesn't re-review already-covered commits — **no new formal verdict is issued**, so the last standing formal reviews remain CHANGES_REQUESTED from both CodeRabbit and you. |
| 28, 05:23 | Mani **closes PR #41**, unmerged, no closing comment. |
| 28, 05:43 | Mani opens **PR #43** from the *same branch* — a redo that explicitly fixes the two must-resolve items. |
| 28, 05:45–06:30 | Four more commits land on that same branch under #43 (including two `coderabbitai[bot]`-authored "apply CodeRabbit auto-fixes" commits), each triggering another `dev` auto-deploy — this is the deploy activity you saw after #41 was "already closed." |

### Your review on #41 — the substance

You requested changes on two blocking items, tied to `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9 ("CPA token held server-side in MRT; never reaches the browser"):

1. **CPA/preview token reaching the browser** — both `contentfulPreview/index.tsx` and `experience/index.tsx` built a client-side Contentful client using the preview token, and `experience/index.tsx`'s `resolvedToken` preferred the preview token even when `isPreview` was false, so normal `/:slug` traffic could hit the preview host on any environment with the token set. You framed it as an intent question for Mani to resolve: either treat client-side preview as a deliberate, documented tradeoff (with a hard non-prod gate) or proxy it server-side per the existing doc.
2. **`/preview` route ungated on production and not `noindex`** — registered unconditionally with SSR, so it was live/crawlable in prod — an SEO and draft-leak risk.

Plus should-fix items (Rules-of-Hooks violation, `console.log`, race condition, duplicated client-creation logic) and one non-blocking note (the unrelated `.mcp.json` `b2c-dx-mcp` addition, pinned to `@latest`, that CodeRabbit flagged as Major — you suggested splitting to its own PR).

You also explicitly cross-checked against a fresh CodeRabbit run and noted where it agreed (all 4 technical issues) versus what only your review caught (the `.docs/` contradiction, the SEO/noindex gap, and that CodeRabbit's own suggested `isPreview ? previewToken : accessToken` diff was a partial mitigation, not a real fix for #1).

### What the 04:28 fix commit actually resolved

Mani's commit `9d0cd8c` fixed the Rules-of-Hooks issue, removed the `console.log`, added the stale-request guard, extracted shared constants, and reverted the unrelated `.mcp.json` change. His accompanying comment argued the client-side token was **intentional by design** (the Live Preview SDK needs the CPA token in-browser for its `postMessage` channel) and called full server-side proxying "outside scope of this sprint," proposing a Contentful preview-secret follow-up instead.

**Not resolved in that commit:** the production-gating/`noindex` ask (item #2) wasn't touched at all, and item #1 only got the partial mitigation you'd already flagged as insufficient. That's almost certainly why #41 was closed rather than pushed further — it was superseded, not fixed.

### PR #43 — the successor (now carrying this work)

Opened from the identical branch, PR #43 addresses exactly the gaps left open on #41:
- `/preview` now **404s when `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_ACCESS_TOKEN` is absent** (non-prod gate), and Experience pages fall back to delivery mode silently with no token.
- **Adds `<Seo noIndex />`** on both preview paths.
- **Updates `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9** to document the client-side token as a deliberate, gated tradeoff — reconciling the doc as you asked.
- Flags that `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` is Tier 1 and expects CODEOWNERS to auto-request `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.

Current state of #43: **open**, `mergeStateStatus: BEHIND`, reviews still outstanding from PWA Squad A/B and Tier-1/Tier-2 Approvers, **CodeRabbit has requested changes twice** (05:48 and 06:22), and the **Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) check is currently failing** — so this isn't merge-ready yet either, just further along than #41 was.

=== .docs/integration/02-contentful.md around 404/security section ===
- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route (which returns 404 when no token is present) and `?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode when no token is present). Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.

25	    client: ContentfulClientApi<any>
26	    slug: string
27	    locale: string
28	    isPreview: boolean
29	}

31	/** Inner component so useFetchBySlug is always called unconditionally at the top level. */
32	const ExperienceFetch = ({client, slug, locale, isPreview}: ExperienceFetchProps) => {
33	    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
34	    const {experience, isLoading, error} = useFetchBySlug({
35	        client: client as any,
36	        slug,
37	        experienceTypeId: EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID,
38	        localeCode: locale,
39	    })

41	    if (isLoading) {
42	        return (

45	            </Box>
46	        )

53	            </Box>
54	        )
55	    }

58

60	        return (
61	            <>
62	                {/* noindex — preview mode serves draft content, must not be indexed */}
63	                <Seo noIndex />
64	                <ContentfulLivePreviewProvider
65	                    locale={locale}
66	                    enableInspectorMode={true}
67	                    enableLiveUpdates={true}
68	                    targetOrigin={CONTENTFUL_LIVE_PREVIEW_ORIGIN}
69	                >
70	                    {root}

72	            </>

76	    return root
77	}
78

80	    slug: string
81	    isPreview?: boolean
82	}
83	
84	const ExperiencePage = ({slug, isPreview = false}: ExperiencePageProps) => {
85	    const {locale: siteLocale} = useMultiSite() as {locale?: {id: string}}
86	    const locale = siteLocale?.id || CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE
87	    const {spaceId, environment, previewAccessToken, accessToken} = getContentfulConfig() ?? {}
88	    const previewUnavailable = isPreview && !previewAccessToken
89	    // Use preview host only when explicitly in preview mode AND a preview token is available.
90	    // Falls back to delivery mode silently when no token is set (non-prod gate).
91	    const effectivePreview = isPreview && !!previewAccessToken
92	    const token = effectivePreview ? previewAccessToken : accessToken
93	    const host = effectivePreview ? CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_HOST : CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_HOST
94	
95	    const client = useMemo(() => {
96	        if (!spaceId || !token) return null
97	        return createClient({space: spaceId, environment, accessToken: token, host})
98	    }, [spaceId, environment, token, host])
99	
100	    if (previewUnavailable) {
101	        return (
102	            <Box p={8}>
103	                <Text color="red.500">
104	                    Preview is not enabled in this environment.
105	                </Text>
106	            </Box>
107	        )
108	    }
109	
110	    if (!client) {
111	        return (
112	            <Box p={8}>
113	                <Text color="red.500">Contentful configuration is missing — cannot render this page.</Text>
114	            </Box>
115	        )
116	    }
117	
118	    return <ExperienceFetch client={client} slug={slug} locale={locale} isPreview={effectivePreview} />
119	}
120	
121	const Experience = () => {
122	    const {pathname, search} = useLocation()
123	    const slug = pathname.slice(1) // strip leading '/'
124	    const isPreview = new URLSearchParams(search).has('preview')
125	
126	    return <ExperiencePage slug={slug} isPreview={isPreview} />
127	}

content.text:
Verdict confirmed with empirical proof, and the investigation turned up something more important than the fix itself. Full findings below.

## Rules-of-Hooks Review — PR #43

### Verdict

**The current branch tip (`bf81428`) is fully Rules-of-Hooks compliant** — both `experience/index.tsx` and `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`. I verified this by running the repo's *own* ESLint over every commit, not by eyeballing. The violation your #41 review flagged was real, regressed once, and is now genuinely fixed.

**But the fix is not the headline.** The headline is *how* it was caught: `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` is configured as an **`error`** in this repo, yet the violation still got committed and deployed to dev — because **nothing in the pipeline runs ESLint.** CodeRabbit was the only thing standing between this bug and `develop`.

### Empirical evidence (repo's own ESLint, via `--stdin-filename`)

| Commit | What it is | `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` |
|---|---|---|
| `4a11982` | State CodeRabbit reviewed at 06:22 | **`105:20 error — React Hook "useMemo" is called conditionally`** |
| `bf81428` | Current tip (after autofix) | **Clean** (105 → 104 problems; the removed one is exactly this) |

The rule lives in the base config at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint/partials/react.js:25` → `'react-hooks/rules-of-hooks': 'error'`. (Note: `exhaustive-deps` is deliberately *off* there, replaced by `use-effect-no-deps`.)

### Full hook audit — every component in the PR

Every hook is called unconditionally at the top, before any early return; no hooks in conditionals, loops, or nested functions. Each component's hook count is invariant across renders:

| Component | Hooks (in order) | Early returns after hooks? | Compliant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `experience` → `ExperienceFetch` | `useFetchBySlug` | 3 returns, all after | ✅ |
| `experience` → `ExperiencePage` | `useMultiSite`, `useMemo` | 2 returns, all after | ✅ *(the one that regressed)* |
| `experience` → `Experience` | `useLocation` | none | ✅ |
| `preview` → `ExperienceView` | `useFetchById` | 3 returns, all after | ✅ |
| `preview` → `ContentfulPreviewPage` | `useMemo`, `useState`, `useState`, `useEffect` | 3 returns, all after | ✅ |
| `preview` → `ContentfulPreview` | `useLocation`, `useMultiSite`, `useServerContext` | 2 returns, all after | ✅ |

The architecture is the *correct* idiomatic pattern: each phase needing its own hooks (client creation → entry-type resolution → fetch) is isolated into its own child component, so the flow is driven by conditional **rendering of children**, never conditional **calling of hooks**. When `isPreview`/`previewUnavailable` toggles, the parent's hook sequence stays fixed; only which child mounts changes — and mount/unmount is not a violation. This is exactly the pattern your #41 review asked for, applied consistently.

### The regression timeline — and the irony

1. `9d0cd8c` (#41 fix) — extracted `ExperienceFetch`, fixing your original `useFetchBySlug`-after-return finding. ✓
2. `b745824` — **introduced the regression.** The commit message (`Update overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`) + `coderabbitai[bot]` co-author is the signature of a web-UI "commit suggestion" click. It applied **CodeRabbit's own 05:48 suggestion** — the `previewUnavailable` explicit-error block (which correctly addressed your "fail explicitly, don't silently fall back to delivery" concern) — but that suggested diff inserted the early `return` **above the existing `useMemo`**, making the hook conditional.
3. `4a11982` — a formatting autofix; **did not touch the hook order**, so the violation persisted. This is what CodeRabbit's 06:22 pass reviewed and flagged **Critical**.
4. `bf81428` — CodeRabbit autofix **moved `useMemo` above the early returns.** Fixed.

So: CodeRabbit *introduced* the violation via a suggestion, then *caught and fixed* it two passes later. That round-trip only worked because a human kept re-triggering reviews — it is not a gate.

### Runtime blast radius (honest characterization)

This wasn't crashing dev. It throws only when `previewUnavailable` flips on an **already-mounted** `ExperiencePage` — i.e. `isPreview` toggles via the URL **and** the CPA token is absent. On dev the token is present, so `previewUnavailable` stays `false` and the hook count never changed there — the broken build ran on dev harmlessly for ~40 min.

The nasty part: the token is deliberately absent on **staging/prod**. So the one place this *would* throw React's "rendered fewer hooks than expected" white-screen is production-like environments — triggered by an in-place `?preview` add/remove on the same `/:slug` instance (React Router re-renders rather than remounts on a query-only change). Low probability (preview links aren't in nav), highest-severity environment. Precisely the latent, test-green, environment-specific failure the rule exists to prevent.

### The process gap (the actionable finding)

I verified all three directly:
- **No workflow runs lint** — `grep -riE "eslint|run lint" .github/workflows/` → nothing.
- **Pre-commit doesn't run lint** — `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` has no eslint/lint step.
- **These files don't even pass `npm run lint` today** — the current tip throws **~102 `prettier/prettier` errors**. I ruled out a harness artifact: the same ESLint harness on the already-merged `develop:overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` returns **0 errors**, so the config resolution is faithful — the Contentful files are genuinely dirty (they use a semicolon-less / no-brace-spacing style the repo's Prettier defaults reject; CodeRabbit noted the semicolon style as a nitpick too).

So a lint-`error`-level rule that would have blocked this at authoring time is wired into neither pre-commit nor CI. **Recommendation:** add a lint job to `qa.yml` (or a pre-commit lint step). It's the cheapest possible catch for this entire bug class — and `.eslintrc.js` / `.github/workflows/` are Tier 1, so that change routes through Integration, which is appropriate given it changes a merge gate. Worth raising on #43's thread since this PR is the concrete example.

### One residual item (not a violation)

`contentfulPreview/index.tsx:117` — the `getEntry` `useEffect` still lists `locale` in its deps, but the effect only resolves a locale-independent content type. Harmless correctness-wise; causes an unnecessary spinner flash on locale change. CodeRabbit flagged it as a nitpick. This is a dependency-array smell, **not** a Rules-of-Hooks issue — and since `exhaustive-deps` is off in this repo, lint won't flag it either way.

content.content:
=== 02-contentful.md lines 44-82 at branch tip (bf81428) ===
## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
        │        CPA token is present the routes fall back to a 404 /
        │        delivery mode. The Live Preview SDK requires the token
        │        in the browser for postMessage-based real-time updates.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.

- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

content.text:
Validated against the actual code. CodeRabbit's finding is correct — and tracing it exposes that the fix it's proposing would quietly lock in an inconsistency. Here's the consolidated picture.

## PR #43 — Re-analysis (tip `bf81428`, unchanged since last pass)

The new full-review (2026-07-29 02:53, CHANGES_REQUESTED, against the current tip) posted **exactly one actionable finding**. No new commits, so my prior code analysis still holds; CI is unchanged (BrowserStack still red, branch still `BEHIND`).

### CodeRabbit's finding — VALID ✅

**Claim (Major):** `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` says `?preview` Experience pages "fall back to Delivery API mode" with no token, but the code no longer does that.

**Verified against `experience/index.tsx`:**
```
88:  const previewUnavailable = isPreview && !previewAccessToken
100:     if (previewUnavailable) {
104:         return … "Preview is not enabled in this environment."   // explicit error — never reaches the delivery client
```
The doc contradicts this in **three places**, all confirmed present at the tip:
- §3 diagram comment (L54-60): *"the routes fall back to a 404 / delivery mode"*
- §4 auth table CPA row (L72-80): *"Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode"*
- §9 security bullet (L128): *"`?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode…)"*

CodeRabbit's read of the code is accurate, its "only `/preview`'s 404 is still accurate" sub-claim is also correct (I re-confirmed `/preview` genuinely does `res.status(404)` + `<Seo noIndex/>`). The finding is real. It's essentially CodeRabbit catching the **doc drift left behind by its own earlier 05:48 suggestion** (the one that changed the code from silent-fallback → explicit error, and in doing so also caused the rules-of-hooks regression we already traced).

### The catch CodeRabbit missed — "update the doc to match" enshrines an inconsistency ⚠️

CodeRabbit's fix is doc-only: *make the doc say what the code does.* But look at what that would be documenting — the two preview entry points behave **differently** in the exact same no-token condition:

| No-token request | Renders | HTTP status | `noindex`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/preview?entry=X` | "Not found." | **404** | **Yes** |
| `/:slug?preview` | "Preview is not enabled…" | **200** | **No** |

So on production (where the CPA token is deliberately absent), `https://www.zimmermann.com/<real-slug>?preview` returns an indexable **HTTP 200** thin error page on a real, crawlable URL — while `/preview` correctly 404s + noindexes. That's the **residual half of your original #41 finding #2** (the noindex/gating ask): `/preview` got fully hardened, the `?preview` error branch didn't. CodeRabbit's doc-only fix would write this inconsistency into the source-of-truth integration doc as if it were intentional.

### The decision buried underneath

Worth naming explicitly, because CodeRabbit's 05:48 suggestion made this call implicitly by invoking the graceful-degradation rule — but that rule is written about *"checkout, payment, or commerce flow"* substitution, not CMS preview overlays. Showing the published page when preview isn't available isn't a dangerous silent substitution; it's arguably the *friendlier* behavior for a stray public hit. So there's a real product choice: **explicit-error** (better for an editor hitting a misconfigured env) vs **delivery-fallback** (better for a stray public `?preview` hit). My recommendation reconciles both.

### Consolidated fix (valid + applicable)

Do the code and doc together rather than doc-only:

1. **Code — `experience/index.tsx` (Tier 4):** make the `previewUnavailable` branch consistent with `/preview` — add `<Seo noIndex/>`, and set a 404 via `useServerContext()` (imported unconditionally at top, same pattern the preview page already uses; keeps hooks compliant). Keeps the editor-friendly explicit message *and* closes the SEO/status gap.
2. **Doc — `02-contentful.md` (not tier-gated; doc-accuracy update):** update all three spots to state both paths fail explicitly — `/preview` → 404, `?preview` → explicit "preview unavailable" — both `noindex`, no delivery-mode fallback. This is cleaner to document *because* the two paths would then behave consistently.

If the team instead prefers doc-only (accept the 200/no-noindex behavior as-is), that's a legitimate call — but it should be a conscious "we're OK with an indexable 200 on prod `?preview` URLs," not an accident of a suggestion, and it still leaves your #41 item #2 only half-closed.

### Everything else — unchanged since last analysis
- **Rules-of-hooks:** compliant at `bf81428` (same commit, still verified). ✅
- **Shared `useContentfulClient` hook (DRY):** still not extracted — CodeRabbit has now stopped re-flagging it, but the duplication is still there.
- **BrowserStack E2E:** still FAILURE — undiagnosed.
- **Branch:** still `BEHIND` develop; still zero human reviews (Tier-1 review on `contentful.ts` still required from someone other than Mani).

Want me to check out the PR branch and implement the consolidated code+doc fix, or leave this as the review write-up to post on the thread?

## Must-fix — correctness & the one valid open CodeRabbit finding

**1. Reconcile the `?preview` no-token behavior (code + doc together).** This is CodeRabbit's 02:53 Major finding *plus* the residual half of the original #41 noindex ask. Two entry points currently disagree in the same no-token state:

|---|---|---|---|

- [ ] **`overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`** (Tier 4) — in the `previewUnavailable` branch (~L100-108): add `<Seo noIndex/>` (already imported, used at L63) and set 404 via `useServerContext()` (import at top, unconditional — same pattern `contentfulPreview` already uses; keeps hooks compliant). Makes both preview paths behave identically.
- [ ] **`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`** (not tier-gated) — fix all **three** stale "delivery-mode fallback" references: §3 diagram comment (L54-60), §4 CPA table row (L72-80), §9 security bullet (L128). State both paths fail explicitly — `/preview`→404, `?preview`→explicit message — both `noindex`.

*Decision point (Mani owns the code + doc):* if he consciously prefers to keep the 200/soft-error and just fix the doc, that's a legitimate call — but it should be deliberate ("we accept an indexable 200 on prod `?preview` URLs"), not left as-is by default. Recommended path is the code+doc fix above.

## Gates Mani must clear (not code, but his to drive)

- [ ] **BrowserStack E2E — currently FAILURE.** Diagnose and fix (or justify); it's the only red check.
- [ ] **Branch is `BEHIND` develop** — update/merge develop in.
- [ ] **Tier-1 review on `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`** — CODEOWNERS-gated to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. GitHub won't accept Mani's own approval even though he's on the team — he needs to request it from **Marcel or Tim**.
- [ ] **Tier-2 / cross-squad review on `overrides/app/routes.tsx`** — needs an approving review from a developer on the *other* squad.
- [ ] **Reply in-thread to each CodeRabbit finding** (AGENTS.md rule) — a fix commit alone doesn't count; CodeRabbit's learning needs the explanation. Applies to the doc finding and anything he skips.

## Should-fix — quality, non-blocking (CodeRabbit raised repeatedly)

- [ ] **Extract a shared `useContentfulClient` hook** — the `getContentfulConfig()`→`useMemo(createClient)` block is still duplicated across both page files. Your original #41 should-fix; flagged 3× since, still open. Also the single natural home for the token/host logic.
- [ ] **`contentfulPreview/index.tsx` L117** — drop `locale` from the `useEffect` dep array (content-type resolution is locale-independent; extra dep causes an unnecessary refetch + spinner flash). Not a hooks violation.
- [ ] **Run `npm run lint:fix`** — these files currently throw ~100 `prettier/prettier` errors (semicolons, brace-spacing). They pass CI only because lint isn't wired into any gate.

## Worth raising (not Mani's to fix alone)

- [ ] **Flag on the PR: lint runs in neither CI nor pre-commit.** That's why a lint-`error`-level rules-of-hooks violation *and* 100+ prettier errors slipped through — CodeRabbit was the only catch. Adding a lint job touches `.github/workflows/` (Tier 1 → Integration), so it's a follow-up, but this PR is the concrete exhibit for proposing it.

content.text:
**BrowserStack diagnosis complete** — it's a pre-existing Tier-1 infra failure, not Mani's code: the repo ships `.browserstack.yml` (dotted) but `browserstack-node-sdk` looks for an undotted `browserstack.yml` (no `BROWSERSTACK_CONFIG_FILE` pointer in `qa.yml`), and the `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`/`ACCESS_KEY` secrets came through empty. It surfaced on #43 (vs SKIPPED on #41) only because #43's body references SFCC-49, flipping the job from "no key → skip" to "key found → run → crash on startup." Both files are Tier 1 (Integration-owned) — out of scope for a feature PR. More below.

Now the code work. Checking out the PR branch (clean tree, no local copy — safe):

git checkout -B feature/storefront-preview-contentful origin/feature/storefront-preview-contentful 2>&1 | tail -3
echo "--- now on ---"
git branch --show-current
git log --oneline -1

70	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
71	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
72	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is only set on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
73	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
74	
75	## 4. Authentication and credentials
76	
77	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
80	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. The `/preview` route returns 404 when token absent; Experience pages with `?preview` fall back to Delivery API mode. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
81	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
82	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
83	
84	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
85	
86	## 5. Data exchanged
87	
88	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
91	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
92	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
93	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
94	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
95	
96	No PII flows through Contentful.
97	
98	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
99	
100	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
101	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
102	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
103	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
104	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
105	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
106	
107	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
108	
109	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
110	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
111	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
112	
113	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
114	
115	| Failure | Behaviour |
116	|---|---|
117	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
118	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
119	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
120	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
121	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
122	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
123	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
124	
125	## 9. Security and privacy
126	
127	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
128	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route (which returns 404 when no token is present) and `?preview` Experience pages (which fall back to Delivery API mode when no token is present). Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
129	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
130	- No PII is handled by Contentful.

23	type ExperienceFetchProps = {
24	    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
25	    client: ContentfulClientApi<any>
26	    slug: string
27	    locale: string
28	    isPreview: boolean
29	}
30	
31	/** Inner component so useFetchBySlug is always called unconditionally at the top level. */
32	const ExperienceFetch = ({client, slug, locale, isPreview}: ExperienceFetchProps) => {
33	    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
34	    const {experience, isLoading, error} = useFetchBySlug({
35	        client: client as any,
36	        slug,
37	        experienceTypeId: EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID,
38	        localeCode: locale,
39	    })
40	
41	    if (isLoading) {
42	        return (
43	            <Box p={8} display="flex" justifyContent="center">
44	                <Spinner size="xl" />
45	            </Box>
46	        )
47	    }
48	
49	    if (error || !experience) {
50	        return (
51	            <Box p={8}>
52	                <Text color="red.500">Page not found.</Text>
53	            </Box>
54	        )
55	    }
56	
57	    const root = <ExperienceRoot experience={experience} locale={locale} />
58	
59	    if (isPreview) {
60	        return (
61	            <>
62	                {/* noindex — preview mode serves draft content, must not be indexed */}
63	                <Seo noIndex />
64	                <ContentfulLivePreviewProvider
65	                    locale={locale}
66	                    enableInspectorMode={true}
67	                    enableLiveUpdates={true}
68	                    targetOrigin={CONTENTFUL_LIVE_PREVIEW_ORIGIN}
69	                >
70	                    {root}
71	                </ContentfulLivePreviewProvider>
72	            </>
73	        )
74	    }
75	
76	    return root
77	}
78	
79	type ExperiencePageProps = {
80	    slug: string
81	    isPreview?: boolean
82	}
83	
84	const ExperiencePage = ({slug, isPreview = false}: ExperiencePageProps) => {
85	    const {locale: siteLocale} = useMultiSite() as {locale?: {id: string}}
86	    const locale = siteLocale?.id || CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE
87	    const {spaceId, environment, previewAccessToken, accessToken} = getContentfulConfig() ?? {}
88	    const previewUnavailable = isPreview && !previewAccessToken
89	    // Use preview host only when explicitly in preview mode AND a preview token is available.
90	    // Falls back to delivery mode silently when no token is set (non-prod gate).
91	    const effectivePreview = isPreview && !!previewAccessToken
92	    const token = effectivePreview ? previewAccessToken : accessToken
93	    const host = effectivePreview ? CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_HOST : CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_HOST
94	
95	    const client = useMemo(() => {
96	        if (!spaceId || !token) return null
97	        return createClient({space: spaceId, environment, accessToken: token, host})
98	    }, [spaceId, environment, token, host])
99	
100	    if (previewUnavailable) {
101	        return (
102	            <Box p={8}>
103	                <Text color="red.500">
104	                    Preview is not enabled in this environment.
105	                </Text>
106	            </Box>
107	        )
108	    }
109	
110	    if (!client) {
111	        return (
112	            <Box p={8}>
113	                <Text color="red.500">Contentful configuration is missing — cannot render this page.</Text>
114	            </Box>
115	        )
116	    }
117	
118	    return <ExperienceFetch client={client} slug={slug} locale={locale} isPreview={effectivePreview} />
119	}
120	
121	const Experience = () => {
122	    const {pathname, search} = useLocation()
123	    const slug = pathname.slice(1) // strip leading '/'
124	    const isPreview = new URLSearchParams(search).has('preview')
125	
126	    return <ExperiencePage slug={slug} isPreview={isPreview} />
127	}

Quick map first — 5 are Mani's, 1 (the last) is really Integration's:

---

### 1. `?preview` on prod shows an indexable error page — *code, `experience/index.tsx`*

- **Problem (ELI5):** There are two "preview" doors into the site. The `/preview` door, when preview isn't allowed, slams shut properly (404, "go away, Google"). The `?preview`-on-a-normal-page door just puts up a paper sign saying "preview not enabled" — but the door's still wide open and says "200 OK, this is a real page."
- **Implication:** On production (no preview token by design), `https://www.zimmermann.com/<real-slug>?preview` returns an **indexable HTTP 200 thin page** on a real, crawlable URL. SEO duplicate/thin-content risk, and it's inconsistent with `/preview`. It's the unfinished half of your original #41 "gate it + noindex it" ask.
- **Proof:** `experience/index.tsx:100-108` — the `previewUnavailable` branch renders only `<Box><Text>`, no `<Seo noIndex/>`, no status. Compare `contentfulPreview/index.tsx:168-180`, which does `res.status(404)` + `<Seo noIndex/>`. The experience file doesn't even import `useServerContext`, so it *can't* set a status today.
- **Fix:** In that branch, add `<Seo noIndex/>` and set 404 via `useServerContext()` (import it, call at top level so hooks stay legal). Now both doors behave identically.

---

### 2. The integration doc describes behavior the code no longer has — *doc, `02-contentful.md`*

- **Problem (ELI5):** The manual still describes the old model of the car. The code was traded in (silent "show the published page" → explicit error), but the doc still says "falls back to delivery mode."
- **Implication:** This doc is the team's source of truth *and* the document that justifies the client-side CPA-token security tradeoff. If it misstates the gating behavior, the next security reviewer / new dev / QA reasons from wrong facts. (AGENTS.md doc-integrity rule.)
- **Proof:** Three stale references at `:59` (diagram), `:80` (§4 CPA table row), `:128` (§9 bullet). Bonus: `:128` also claims *"Both preview paths are `noindex`"* — which is **false until Fix 1 lands**.
- **Fix:** Update all three to: both paths fail explicitly (`/preview`→404, `?preview`→explicit message), both `noindex`, no delivery fallback. Do it **with** Fix 1 so code and doc agree and that "both noindex" line becomes true.

---

### 3. The Contentful client is built twice by copy-paste — *code, both pages (DRY)*

- **Problem (ELI5):** The same recipe for "make the Contentful client" is written out in two different kitchens. Change the recipe in one, the other quietly serves the old dish.
- **Implication:** This is the exact block holding the **security-sensitive token/host choice** (preview vs delivery). If someone later hardens one copy and forgets the other, the two preview entry points diverge — possibly unsafely. CodeRabbit has flagged it 3×.
- **Proof:** `createClient(` appears once in `experience/index.tsx` and once in `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`; `useContentfulClient` = 0 (doesn't exist). Both blocks are `getContentfulConfig()` → `useMemo(() => createClient(...))`.
